sections.title: Overview
lines: Buttons start actions: send an inquiry, save a search, apply filters. Three variants set the emphasis, from the dark blue primary to the quiet tertiary. Three sizes (32, 40 and 48px) replace the three heights and two corner radii AcmeCo uses today.

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  Primary: the one main action in a region, such as "Contact broker" on a listing. Use at most one per region.
•  Secondary: an alternative to the primary action, such as "Save search" beside "Search".
•  Tertiary: low-emphasis actions, such as "Clear filters", or actions repeated in lists.
•  With href: when the button takes the user somewhere ("View documents"). It renders a real link, so it opens in a new tab and screen readers announce it as a link.

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  For navigation inside text, use a link instead.
•  For an icon on its own, use IconButton, which requires an accessible label.
•  Don't put two primary buttons side by side; make one secondary.
•  Don't disable a button to stop a form being sent before it's complete. Let the user press it and show what's missing.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  Built on React Aria's Button: Enter and Space press it; mouse, touch and keyboard all fire onPress.
•  The label is the accessible name. Icons are hidden from screen readers.
•  Focus shows a 2px blue ring, offset 2px so it never touches dark blue.
•  Loading keeps keyboard focus, ignores presses and tells screen readers the button is busy. It never uses the disabled attribute, which would drop focus mid-action.
•  Disabled buttons can't be focused, so explain nearby why the action isn't available.
•  Every variant and state meets WCAG AA contrast (checked in CI): primary text 10.98:1 at rest, secondary 10.98:1, tertiary 17.04:1.
•  Targets are 32px or taller, above the 24px minimum (WCAG 2.5.8).

sections.title: Content
lines: •  Start with a verb and say what happens: "Contact broker", not "Submit" or "OK".
•  Sentence case. No more than three or four words.
•  Keep the same label for the same action everywhere.

sections.title: Evidence
lines: •  Observed (audit family F03): 207 instances, 12 variants, 26 distinct designs. The dark blue primary appears in 3 heights (33, 43 and 48px) and 2 radii (2 and 4px), with grey-filled, outlined and blue text-only variants alongside.

•  legacy-named: --legacy-cta-font-size 18px, --legacy-cta-font-weight 400, --legacy-cta-line-height 1.5, --legacy-cta-padding-inline 16px, --legacy-cta-radius 4px, --legacy-cta-transition 0.15s, --legacy-color-brand-hover. All kept.
•  Now: 3 variants × 3 sizes, one radius, and every state defined (hover, pressed, focus, disabled, loading), none of which were captured on the live site.

sections.title: Overview
lines: An icon-only button for compact, familiar actions: save a listing, go to the next photo, share, close. It always has an accessible name: label is required, and the code won't compile without it. Three variants cover where it sits: plain in toolbars and cards, overlay on photos, primary for the search submit.

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  Plain: familiar actions in toolbars, cards and headers (share, close).
•  Overlay: controls on top of photos (carousel arrows, save on a listing photo). The translucent white circle keeps the icon readable on any image.
•  Primary: the search submit inside the location field. Use shape="circle" inside a pill-shaped field (the hero search), where square corners would poke past the curve.
•  As a toggle (isSelected + onChange): actions that switch on and off, like save. The icon turns dark blue and fills when on, and screen readers hear "pressed".
•  With href: when it navigates. It renders a real link.

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  When the icon isn't universally understood. Use a Button with a label instead.
•  For the main action in a region. Use a primary Button: words beat icons for important actions.
•  Don't use a toggle for actions that happen once (like "share"); use a plain button.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  label is required and becomes the accessible name ("Save listing", "Next photo"). Say what it does, not what it shows ("Close", not "X").
•  Built on React Aria: Enter and Space press it. Toggles use aria-pressed, so screen readers announce "pressed" or "not pressed".
•  Focus: the blue 2px ring for plain and primary; over photos, AcmeCo's own double ring (white inside, ink outside) so it shows on any image.
•  Selected isn't shown by colour alone: the icon also fills (WCAG 1.4.1).
•  Icons meet 3:1 against their background in every state (checked in CI), down to 4.07:1 for a saved icon on the overlay over the darkest photo.
•  Targets are 32, 40 or 48px, above the 24px minimum (WCAG 2.5.8).
•  Sighted mouse users don't see the label. A tooltip component would show it on hover; that's planned for later, so keep to universally understood icons until then.

sections.title: Content
lines: •  Labels start with a verb or name the action: "Save listing", "Next photo", "Share listing", "Close dialog".
•  Include what it acts on when the screen has several: "Save 233 S Wacker Dr", not just "Save".
•  For a toggle, keep the same label in both states; the pressed state is announced for you.

sections.title: Evidence
lines: •  Observed (audit family F04): 107 instances, 14 variants, 14 distinct designs. No-container icons in five greys and blacks plus a failing blue (#0888ba, 4.0:1); translucent white circles at 85% and 60%; grey-outlined pills; dark blue filled.
•  Accessibility: 481 of 533 icon-only buttons on AcmeCo had no aria-label (other naming methods weren't measured). Here a missing label is a compile error, tested in IconButton.typetest.tsx.
•  AcmeCo's own focus ring (white 2px inside, ink 2px outside) was captured in the audit's shadow data and is used for the overlay variant.
•  Now: 3 variants × 3 sizes, one ink colour, 85% white over photos, and every state defined, including selected.

components.name: Link
components.gridNote: Context = the body text style around the link (a link inherits its size and weight). Inverse links sit on a dark panel, as in their story.

sections.title: Overview
lines: Links take people somewhere: another page, a section, an outside site. Four variants replace the 21 link styles on AcmeCo today. Links take their size and weight from the text around them, so they add no new type styles.

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  Inline: inside sentences ("See the building's floor plans"). Always underlined.
•  Standalone: on its own line or beside a heading ("View all office listings").
•  Subtle: listing titles in cards and navigation items, where the context already says "this is clickable". Ink colour, underlined on hover. Keeps AcmeCo's familiar bold black titles.
•  Inverse: on dark surfaces such as the auction banner or a dark footer.
•  External: set external when the link leaves AcmeCo or opens a new tab.
•  With icon, a view switch that has its own address: the search results' "Map" (map icon) and "Gallery" (grid icon). The icon is decorative; the text names the link.

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  For actions that change something (save, send, apply), use a Button.
•  For a link that should look like a button ("View documents"), use a Button with href.
•  Don't use subtle links inside body text: without the underline and colour, they're invisible there.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  A real link (<a href>), built on React Aria: Enter follows it, and it works with middle-click and "open in new tab".
•  Inline links are always underlined. Link blue is only 2.50:1 against ink body text, below the 3:1 that would let colour alone mark a link (WCAG 1.4.1), so the underline does that job.
•  Link text meets AA everywhere it's used: blue 6.80:1 on white and 6.13:1 on grey, ink 17.04:1, white 12.71:1 on the navy banner.
•  Focus shows the 2px blue ring, or a white ring on dark surfaces (the blue is only 1.87:1 on navy).
•  External links add an icon and "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers, so the new tab isn't a surprise.

sections.title: Content
lines: •  Say where the link goes: "View all office listings in Chicago", not "Click here" or "More".
•  Keep link text unique on a page when the destinations differ: several "Learn more" links read the same to a screen reader listing the page's links.
•  Don't put a full stop inside the link text.

sections.title: Evidence
lines: •  Observed (audit family F01): 3,295 instances, 21 variants, 44 distinct designs: the highest volume and the most variation in the audit after the property card.
•  Link colours observed: four blues (#0559b3, #0888ba failing AA at 4.0:1, #0c6cc4, #0056b6), plus near-black bold links, greys, white and dark blue.
•  Now: one blue (#0559b3, the most used, 1,007 elements in 11 experiences), ink for subtle links, white for inverse, and every state defined.

components.name: Breadcrumbs
components.gridNote: Shown 560px wide; narrower, the trail wraps and the current page drops to its own line. Strip: a listing and the end of the results. Plain: a step back (a broker's page). Edit the Crumb and Current layers per page; the current page is never a link.

sections.title: Overview
lines: Where a page sits in the site: a trail of links from the widest page to the current one, which comes last and isn't a link. AcmeCo shows one under a listing's title and at the end of the search results; its broker page has a one-step version back to the listing. The three screens' gap logs all asked for it (decision 47).

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  At the top of a listing (appearance="strip", AcmeCo's light grey strip), and at the end of a results list.
•  On a page reached from another one, to go back a level (a broker's page: the listing, then the broker), with appearance="plain".

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  Not as the site's main navigation: that's the GlobalHeader's NavigationBar.
•  Not for steps in a process (a form in parts): that's a step indicator, which the system doesn't have yet.
•  Don't add the current page as a link to itself.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  A navigation named "Breadcrumb" holding an ordered list, built on React Aria's Breadcrumbs: screen readers announce how many items there are and where the reader is.

•  The current page is plain text, marked with aria-current="page", so it's announced as the current page. AcmeCo links the ZIP code inside the current item; here the current item is text only, so the trail never ends in a link to somewhere else.
•  The slashes are drawn by CSS with empty alternative text, so they aren't read out.
•  Links are AcmeCo's blue, underlined on hover; text on the strip passes AA: link blue 6.46:1, the grey current page 5.48:1 and the ink slashes 16.18:1 on #f9f9f9.

sections.title: Content
lines: •  Use the names AcmeCo uses: the space type ("Office Spaces"), the state, the city, then the page itself (an address, or "Office Spaces for Lease in Denver, CO").
•  Keep each label short; the current page may be longer and wraps on phones.

sections.title: Evidence
lines: •  OBSERVED (audit captures, property detail at 1700px and 400px): a #f9f9f9 strip with 1px #dddddd lines above and below, 14/18 text, blue links (#0559b3) without underlines, ink slashes about 4px from the words, the current address in grey (#63666a); on the phone the address wraps onto its own line.
•  OBSERVED (map search, the list column's end): the same strip, 15px text, the current page in black. Now one size (14px) and one colour (grey) for both (decision 47).
•  Now: 14/21 (decision 9), the system's default border (#e5e5e5) and page gutter (16px).

sections.title: Overview
lines: A labelled field for typing: a name, an email address, a message to a broker. One shape (outlined, 4px corners) replaces the five AcmeCo uses today. It shares its label, hint, error and border with every other form control, so they all look and behave alike.

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  Short text: name, email, phone (type sets the right mobile keyboard).
•  Longer text: set multiline for a message, and maxLength to show a live count.
•  Read-only values someone may want to copy: set isReadOnly.
•  The pill shape and lg size are for the hero location search only.

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  Choosing from a known list: use Select.
•  Searching: use SearchField, which adds a clear button and Escape to clear.
•  Don't use the placeholder as the label: it disappears as soon as someone types.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  The label is always present and is the field's accessible name. hideLabel hides it visually only, and only where the purpose is obvious from context.
•  Built on React Aria: the hint and error are linked to the field, so screen readers read them when it's focused.
•  Errors use three cues, not colour alone: the error red, a thicker border, and an icon with a message.
•  Required fields show an asterisk; screen readers hear "required" from the field itself.
•  Text is 16px or larger (which also stops iOS zooming in on focus); placeholder 5.77:1; the border 3.81:1 against white (WCAG 1.4.11).
•  The character counter is visual; the limit is announced once, in the hint, not on every keystroke.

sections.title: Content
lines: •  Labels are short nouns: "Email", "Phone (optional)". Mark optional fields, not just required ones, when most are required.
•  Hints say what's expected: "We'll only use this to reply to you."
•  Error messages say how to fix it: "Enter an email address like name@company.com", not "Invalid input".

sections.title: Evidence
lines: •  Observed (audit family F08): 177 instances, 5 variants, 9 distinct designs: a grey outline at 2px corners (108), a white square, a grey-outlined pill at 40px, a white pill at 48px (hero search), and a grey fill at 4px, 38px tall.
•  Accessibility: the observed control border #b1b3b0 is 2.11:1 against white, below the 3:1 a field boundary needs.
•  Now: one outlined shape at 4px with a 3.81:1 border, 40 and 48px heights, the pill kept only for the hero, and every state defined (hover, focus, invalid, disabled, read-only).

sections.title: Overview
lines: A search box: a TextField with a clear button (AcmeCo's filled dark circle with a white cross), Escape to clear and Enter to search. With showSubmit it adds the dark blue Search button inside its end edge, as in the hero location search.

sections.title: When to use

•  The hero search: size="lg", shape="pill", showSubmit, and hideLabel (the purpose is obvious there).

•  The results search, proposed (decision 45): shape="pill", showSubmit and startIcon={<Navigation />}: the location arrow and the hero's dark blue Search button, so searching again is as obvious on the results as on the home page.
•  The results search as AcmeCo has it today (decision 42): the same with submitAppearance="icon" (a plain dark blue magnifier). Use it to show AcmeCo as it is.

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  Filtering a short list that's already on screen: a Select or Chips may be clearer.
•  Free text that isn't a search (a message): use TextField.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  Built on React Aria's SearchField: it's announced as a search box; Escape clears it; Enter runs the search.
•  The clear button is labelled "Clear search" and only appears when there's text to clear. Its target is 24px (WCAG 2.5.8).
•  The submit button is an IconButton labelled "Search".
•  Same label, border, focus and contrast rules as TextField.

sections.title: Content

•  Keep the placeholder as an example, not as the only label.

sections.title: Overview
lines: AcmeCo's search-bar pills. FilterButton is the pill: a filter's name (or its value once set), an optional icon and count (All Filters: sliders and a blue "2"), and a chevron when it opens a panel. FilterMenu is a FilterButton that opens a panel of choices (a Popover) and, once set, shows its value and clears in place ("Office, Coworking ✕"). Same height, shape and type as the compact Select beside them, so the whole bar is one family (decision 40). Found missing by the search results screen (gaps 1–3).

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  FilterMenu for each filter in a search bar: a list of choices (CheckboxGroup), a range (two TextFields), a single choice.

•  Pass value once it's set: one choice by name ("Office"), "Multiple" for two or more (the chips under the bar list them), a range with its unit ("$20–$40 /SF/YR"), and onClear so the pill clears in place.
•  FilterButton with count and hasMenu={false} for All Filters, opening a Dialog with every filter; on phones use iconOnly (a round button with the count over its corner, as AcmeCo's).
•  Below 768px every pill is AcmeCo's phone size (40px, 16px text, no chevron); put them in a Stack with scrollBelow="md" so they stay on one line and scroll sideways.

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  Not for choosing one value from a short list where a Select fits ("For Lease"): use the compact Select.
•  Not as a page's main action: use Button.
•  Don't put more than a few words in a set pill; the chips under the bar can list everything.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  A real button that says it opens a panel and whether it's open (React Aria); the panel is named by the filter's label, takes focus, and Escape or a click outside closes it and returns focus to the pill.
•  The clear button is its own button ("Clear Rent"), beside the pill's text, 24px (the target minimum).
•  The count is read as part of the name ("All Filters, 2 applied"); the blue circle itself is hidden from screen readers.
•  A set pill is marked by its dark border and its value, not by colour alone. Contrast: text 17.04:1 on white and 15.35:1 on the light grey; the border 3.81:1; the count's white on blue 6.80:1.

sections.title: Content
lines: •  Name filters as AcmeCo does: "Space Use", "Rent", "Size", "All Filters".

•  A set value stays short: one choice by name, "Multiple" for several (AcmeCo joins them with commas, which outgrows the pill; the chips say which), ranges with a dash and the unit ("$20–$40 /SF/YR", "5,000+ SF").

sections.title: Evidence

•  OBSERVED (a phone screenshot, 2026-10-11): on phones 40px pills with 16px text and no chevrons, in one row; All Filters as a round sliders button with the count over its edge (decision 42).
•  OBSERVED (owner's desktop screenshots, 2026-10-11): 40px pills with 16px text on desktop too (decision 45).

•  Now: 40px pills with 16px text at every width, as the compact Select (decision 45; decision 40 had made both 32px / 14px); the control border (#808386, 3:1); weight 400 (decision 4); a 24px clear button; panels 280px.

sections.title: Overview
lines: A few icon buttons where exactly one is chosen, for a view or layout setting that applies at once: the search results' map placement (map on the left, or map on top). It's a proposal for AcmeCo (decision 45). Map placement is a choice between two tasks: reading listings beside a tall map, or seeing more of a wide map with cards in rows below it. It's drawn in AcmeCo's own selected style, the same light blue fill and 2px link-blue border as ChoiceCards.

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  Two to four settings that change how something is shown, where an icon reads quickly (a layout, a view density).
•  Where the change applies straight away and can be undone by choosing again.

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  Settings that need words to tell apart: a TabSelector or ChoiceCards.
•  Moving to another page or view with its own address: a Link (the results' "Map" / "Gallery" switch is a link).
•  Filtering content: FilterButton / FilterMenu.
•  Several settings on at once: a CheckboxGroup.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  React Aria ToggleButtonGroup with single selection, which it exposes as a radio group named by label: one Tab stop, arrow keys move between the buttons and Space or Enter chooses, so looking at another option doesn't change the layout; each button is a radio named by its option's label and announced as checked when chosen.
•  One is always chosen (disallowEmptySelection): pressing the chosen button again leaves it chosen.
•  Each label also shows as a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus, so sighted users don't have to guess what an icon means. Without it, the names would reach screen readers only.
•  The chosen button has a 2px border as well as the fill, so it isn't shown by colour alone (blue border 6.80:1 on white). Icons are ink: 15.35:1 or more on white, grey and light blue.

sections.title: Content

sections.title: Overview
lines: Checkboxes let people pick any number of options (space use, amenities), or confirm one thing ("Email me new listings like this"). It's already AcmeCo's most consistent control, so its look is kept; the border is darkened to pass contrast, and checked becomes the dark blue fill with a white check. CheckboxGroup gives a set of checkboxes one label, hint and error.

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  Any number of options from a short list: a CheckboxGroup with a label ("Space use").
•  A single yes/no choice that takes effect when a form is sent: one Checkbox.
•  "Select all" over a partly checked list: isIndeterminate shows a dash.

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  Exactly one choice from a few: a TabSelector, or a radio group (later).
•  Exactly one choice from many: Select.
•  A setting that takes effect immediately: a switch (not in v1).

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  Built on React Aria: a real checkbox input inside a label, so the whole label is clickable and Space toggles it.
•  In a group, screen readers hear the group's label with each option ("Space use, group. Office, checkbox, checked").
•  Checked is the dark blue fill and the white check mark, not colour alone; indeterminate is a dash and is announced as "mixed".
•  Contrast: the unchecked border is 3.81:1 against white (AcmeCo's current #b1b3b0 is 2.11:1, below the 3:1 needed); checked dark blue 10.98:1; check mark 10.98:1 or more.
•  Each row is at least 24px tall (WCAG 2.5.8).
•  A group error shows an icon and a message linked to the group, and every box gets a red border.

sections.title: Content
lines: •  Labels are short and parallel: "Office", "Retail", "Industrial".
•  For a single checkbox, say what checking it does: "Email me new listings like this".
•  Group errors say what's needed: "Choose at least one space use".

sections.title: Evidence

•  Accessibility: that grey is 2.11:1 against white, below the 3:1 a checkbox boundary needs.
•  Now: the same look with a 3.81:1 border and 4px corners; checked, indeterminate, hover, pressed, focus, invalid and disabled all defined.

sections.title: Overview
lines: A button that opens a list to pick one option. Two appearances: field, for forms, looks and behaves like TextField (it shares its tokens); compact, a 32px pill for sort and filter triggers, sits beside filter chips. Every dropdown on AcmeCo today is custom-built; this one gets the keyboard and screen reader behaviour custom dropdowns usually miss.

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  One choice from about 5 to 15 options: property type, sort order, price range.
•  Field in forms (with a label above). Compact for sorting and filtering results, where the trigger shows its label ("Sort") until a choice is made.

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  Two to four options, all worth seeing at once: a TabSelector.
•  Several choices: a CheckboxGroup.
•  Very long lists that people search (cities, addresses): a search field with suggestions (later).
•  Navigation menus: a menu button (later), not a Select.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  Built on React Aria's Select: announced as a button that opens a list box; arrow keys move through options; typing a letter jumps to it; Enter or Space selects; Escape closes; focus returns to the trigger.
•  The label is always the accessible name, even on compact triggers (where it's hidden visually and shown as the trigger text).
•  The selected option is shown by a check mark and semibold text, not colour alone.
•  Hint and error are linked to the trigger; errors use colour, a thicker border, an icon and a message.
•  Options are 40px tall; the list scrolls after about eight.
•  Contrast: option text 17.04:1, 15.35:1 on the hover row; the trigger border 3.81:1.

sections.title: Content
lines: •  Field labels are short nouns ("Property type"); compact labels say what they control ("Sort", "Price").
•  Option labels are short, parallel and in a sensible order (by size, by price, or alphabetical).
•  Placeholders are prompts ("Select a property type"), never the only label.

•  Now: one field trigger matching TextField (40 or 48px, the 3.81:1 border) and one compact trigger (a 32px pill), with a single list style.

lines: •  Choosing the search mode or listing type at the top of a panel whose content depends on it.

•  Subtle: the same label on a white or grey surface.

•  Meaning never relies on colour alone: the text says what the badge means.

sections.title: Overview
lines: A modal dialog: it blocks the page until it's closed. Header with a required title and a Close button, a body that scrolls, and an optional footer for actions. Two sizes; full screen on phones. Used by sign-in, the contact form and the filters panel.

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  A short task that must be finished or dismissed before going back to the page: contact a broker, sign in, set filters.
•  Put it in a DialogTrigger with the button that opens it; or control it with isOpen and onOpenChange.
•  md (500px) for single-column forms; lg (768px) for two columns or many controls (sign-in, filters).

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  Anything that doesn't need to block the page: use inline content, a popover (Select) or a new page.
•  Long reading or multi-step flows: give them a page.
•  Not for confirmations or alerts yet (alertdialog): none were observed on AcmeCo; add one when a flow needs it.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  The title names the dialog ("Contact broker, dialog"). AcmeCo's captured dialogs have no name, and 7 of 10 aren't marked as dialogs at all.
•  Focus moves into the dialog, stays inside until it closes, then returns to the button that opened it. The page behind can't be scrolled, clicked or reached by screen readers.

•  Escape and the Close button (labelled; AcmeCo's are unnamed icons) always close it. Clicking the backdrop closes it too, except where isDismissable={false}: use that for any dialog holding a form, so a stray click doesn't lose typed input (decision 28).
•  The fade is skipped for people who ask for reduced motion.

sections.title: Content
lines: •  Title: what the dialog is for, in a few words ("Contact broker", "Log in or sign up"). Sentence case.
•  Footer: one primary action, named for what it does ("Send message", not "OK"); a secondary action to its left if needed.
•  Keep the body short; if it scrolls a lot, it may want to be a page.

sections.title: Evidence
lines: •  Observed (audit F31; captured CSS of AcmeCo's sign-in, contact broker and filters dialogs): one modal system styled three ways: 768px / 8px corners / soft shadow (sign-in, the newest), 500px / 4px / grey glow with a sticky footer (contact), 852px / 4px / grey border (filters); centred titles and a 60% black backdrop on all; on a phone, contact and filters go full screen while sign-in runs off the screen.

•  Now (decision 28): the sign-in look for all (8px, shadow.raised), two sizes (500 / 768px), the title in the heading-3 style, left-aligned as a proposed polish (AcmeCo centres dialog titles; decision 28, C), a sticky footer, full screen at 768px and below, named dialog and Close button.

sections.title: Overview
lines: The building blocks of AcmeCo's listing card ("card"), each usable on its own so the property detail page and contact flow can reuse them: PropertyMedia (photos, previous / next, save, labels), PropertyHeader (title and address | size and city), PropertyFacts (price first, then facts, with an optional description), PropertyPrice, and BrokerIdentity (company logo and up to three brokers). sections.title: When to use
lines: •  Inside PropertyCard (most of the time).
•  On their own where a page needs one piece: the price on the detail page (PropertyPrice size="prominent"), the broker block in the contact module, the photo carousel at the top of a listing.

sections.title: Overview
lines: A listing in search results: AcmeCo's card. AcmeCo sells listing tiers, and the tier decides how much the card shows, so PropertyCard takes AcmeCo's own tier (1, 2, 3). Every tier shares the same parts (see Property parts), type scale, container and click behaviour.
Tier: Layout
1: Header row, full-width photo, facts | description, logo and up to three brokers
2: Header row, then photo | facts, description, logo above the brokers. Stacks on narrow cards.
3: Compact: photo | title, address, city, facts | company logo. No description or broker photos.

sections.title: On phones
lines: Below 768px the card is flat and edge to edge, with a grey band under it (put the list in a Bleed with gap={{ base: 'none', md: 'lg' }}); on a narrow card the header stays side by side (the right column cut short with an ellipsis), the facts stay beside the description, and the brokers show as photos without names (still read out), as on AcmeCo's phone (decision 42).

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  Search results, in the list and the map sidebar.
•  Anywhere a listing is offered as one item among many (saved listings, "similar listings").

•  With onAsk (a proposal, decision 45), a sparkle button on the photo beside Save, named "Ask AcmeCo about {listing}": the page opens the Assistant with a question about the listing (Assistant question).

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  The property detail page: use the parts on their own (PropertyMedia, PropertyPrice, BrokerIdentity).
•  Auctions cards and the homepage "Trending" card: they aren't in v1 and need their own variants.
•  Don't choose the tier for looks: it reflects what the advertiser bought.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  One link per card: the title. It is stretched over the whole card, so clicking anywhere opens the listing, while keyboard and screen-reader users meet one link, not several anonymous ones. When it has focus, the whole card shows the focus ring.
•  The save toggle and photo arrows sit above the link and work on their own ("Save Larkspur Commons", "Next photo").

•  The card is an article named by its title, which is a heading (headingLevel, h3 by default under the results' h2). The title comes first in reading order in every tier, even where the photo comes first on screen.
•  In tier 2 with several brokers only initials show, as AcmeCo shows only photos; the names are still read out.
•  Layout follows the card's own width (container queries), so the same card works in the list, the map sidebar and on a phone.

sections.title: Content
lines: •  Title: the property's name, or its street address if it has none.
•  Facts follow the price: "Built in 1963", "253 - 8,024 SF"; tier 3 adds "4 Spaces Available".
•  Descriptions are cut to three lines; the full text belongs on the detail page.

sections.title: Evidence
lines: •  Observed (audit F28, captured DOM of the results list and map view): card tier1/tier2/tier3 with contact-count-1/2/3; map view 670px wide: tier 1 photo 668 x 370px, tier 2 photo 360px beside 308px of details, tier 3 photo 290px with a 100px logo column; 1px #e2e2e2 border, a 0 1px 4px 2px shadow and square corners; 20px side padding.
•  Now: 8px corners (decision 26), 16px padding, one type scale in every view, the price first in the facts (decision 27), one stretched link and a card-wide focus ring, labelled photo controls.
•  The full-width list view stretches the tier 1 photo into a 1703 x 212px banner; the card keeps the map view's shape at every width.

sections.title: Overview
lines: Label / value rows: AcmeCo's property facts ("Building Size 22,400 SF"). The audit found seven designs for this one row on property pages (F21); this is one. It closes the property page's Property Facts gap and fills the space cards on phones (decision 47).

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  For facts about one thing, each a short label and a short value: a property's size, type and year, a space's size, rate and use.
•  columns={2} for a longer list in a wide column: two facts on a row from 560px, one below that, as on AcmeCo's phone.

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  Not to compare several things fact by fact (all the spaces in a building): that's a table.
•  Not for long text; a value is a word, a number or a short phrase.
•  Not for form fields: those are TextField, Select and the rest.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  A description list (dl): screen readers announce it as a list and read each label with its value.
•  Labels are the secondary grey (#63666a, 5.77:1 on white, 5.20:1 on the grey band) and values ink (17.04:1), both 18px; the colour sets the label apart, not a thin weight.
•  The rows follow reading order, so two columns read left to right, then down.

sections.title: Content

sections.title: Overview
lines: A surface that groups related content: AcmeCo's grey-edged panels. The broker page puts its Property Types and Markets, Bio and Listings in them; the property page puts small facts in outlined boxes. The three screens' gap logs asked for it (decision 47).

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  To group content that belongs together and sits beside other groups: a broker's panels (appearance="raised"), a listing's facts or one space (appearance="outline").
•  With heading when the group has a name: the card becomes a section named by it.
•  With actions for what to do with the content ("Details").

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  Not for a listing in a results list: that's PropertyCard.
•  Not around a whole page section that already has a heading and sits on the page: a card around everything is no grouping at all.
•  Don't nest cards.
•  Don't make the whole card a link or button; put the action in actions.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  With a heading, the card is a section labelled by it, so screen readers list it among the page's regions and read its name. Set headingLevel to fit the page's outline; the look doesn't change.
•  The edge is decorative (#e5e5e5): the heading and the content carry the meaning, so it needs no contrast ratio.
•  The raised card's shadow is decoration too; the edge stays, so the card's shape doesn't rely on the shadow.

sections.title: Content
lines: •  Keep headings short and plain ("Bio", "Property Facts", "Suite 300").
•  Put the most useful line first; a card is scanned, not read.

sections.title: Evidence
lines: •  OBSERVED (broker page, 1700px and 400px): AcmeCo's own lnc-card: white, 1px #eeeeee edge, 4px corners, 30px padding (20px on the phone), a soft shadow (rgba(119,119,119,0.07) 0 2px 22px 10px), 15px between cards, 22px headings.
•  OBSERVED (property page, F26.4): outlined boxes with a 1px #e5e5e5 edge, 8px corners and 16px padding.
•  Now: one edge grey (#e5e5e5), 8px corners (decision 26: surfaces), 32px / 16px padding (the 4px grid and the gutter), the system's card shadow (decision 11), 20px headings (heading-3).

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  To compare several things fact by fact: the spaces in a building (Space, Size, Rental Rate, Space Use, Available).
•  With onRowAction when each row has more to show: pressing the row, or its Details button, opens it.

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  Not for facts about one thing: that's FactList.
•  Not on phones: five columns don't fit 375px. Show each row as a Card with a FactList there, as AcmeCo's phone listing does.
•  Not for layout. A table is for data with column headings.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  Built on React Aria's Table: real column headings, and one row-header column (Space), so as a screen reader moves between cells it announces the column heading and the row's name (its Space) with each value. AcmeCo's version is built from lists with no headings, and its chevron can't take focus.

•  Arrow keys move between rows and cells; Enter on a row opens it, as pressing it does. The Details button is a real button inside the row, named for its row ("Details for Floor 2, Suite 200": the space's name is screen-reader-only text).
•  Name the table with labelledBy (its section heading's id) or label.
•  The header bar is ink on #ededed (14.55:1), rows are ink on white, and a hovered row is ink on #f3f3f3 (15.35:1). The focus ring sits inside the row (6.13:1 on the hover grey).

sections.title: Content
lines: •  Use AcmeCo's column headings ("Space", "Size", "Rental Rate", "Space Use", "Available").
•  Keep cells short: the details belong in the opened view.

sections.title: Evidence

sections.title: Overview
lines: AcmeCo's guest contact form ("Contact Broker"): first and last name, email, phone with an optional extension, an optional space size, and a message prefilled with the listing's name. It opens in a Dialog that a stray click can't close (decision 28), and anyone can send it without an account (the benchmark lesson 10). After sending, it confirms who the message went to.

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  From a listing: the Message button in the ContactModule, or "Contact broker" anywhere a listing offers it.
•  Put it in a DialogTrigger with the button that opens it, or control it with isOpen / onOpenChange.
•  Connect onSubmit to the real service; it receives the values only when they're valid.

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  Not as a sign-up form, and don't make signing in a condition for sending (the benchmark's sign-up wall is a weakness, not a model).
•  Don't add fields: every extra one is a reason not to send. Each addition is a product decision.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  Every field has a real label (AcmeCo's names are bold text that isn't connected to its box, so screen readers announce "edit text").
•  Required and optional are both said in words: required fields are announced as required (the asterisk is visual only), optional ones say "(optional)" in their label.
•  On send, each problem appears under its field and is read with it; focus moves to the first field with a problem; nothing typed is cleared. A fixed field clears its message as you type.
•  The confirmation is announced and takes focus; Done closes the dialog and returns focus to the button that opened it.
•  The message counter is announced ("84 / 400").

sections.title: Content
lines: •  Keep AcmeCo's field names and order; "First name" in sentence case.
•  Error messages say what to do: "Enter your phone number.", "Enter an email address like name@example.com."
•  The terms note and links are placeholder wording here; AcmeCo's legal team owns the real text. The reCAPTCHA disclosure is left out (a third-party service).
•  Open question for AcmeCo: phone is required, as today (decision 30). Asking for fewer details may bring more messages; that's a business decision.

sections.title: Evidence
lines: •  Observed (audit capture of the contact broker dialog): First Name * and Last Name * side by side (222px each); Email *; Phone * (302px) and Ext (optional, 142px); "How much space do you need? (optional)" with "Select Size"; Message * prefilled, "84 out of 400"; the automatic-account note with Terms of Use and Privacy Notice; a reCAPTCHA disclosure; a dark blue 47px "Contact Broker" in a sticky footer. No <label> elements; required shown only by a dark blue asterisk; 42px inputs with thin (100) text and #b2b2b2 borders (2.2:1).

•  Now (decision 30): the same fields, order and layout on the system's fields (40px, 3:1 borders, regular text), real labels, required and optional in words, validation with focus, a "Message sent" state (PROPOSED), in the 500px dialog with its sticky footer.

lines: AcmeCo's "Log In/Sign Up" dialog: enter an email to log in or create a free account, or continue with another service, beside a short promo carousel saying why to sign up. It opens when an action needs an account, such as Save results on search results or Log in in the contact form.

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  When someone tries something that needs an account (save results, save a search, track a property).
•  Put it in a DialogTrigger with the control that opens it, or control it with isOpen / onOpenChange.

•  onContinue(email) receives a valid address; the next step (password or new account) is the caller's. onProvider(name) receives the chosen option; providers lists the options with their placeholder marks.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  The email field has a real label and is announced as required (AcmeCo's "Email" is plain text above the box). Continue checks it, explains a problem under the field and moves focus there.

•  Other options keep AcmeCo's round buttons, each named "Continue with Google", "Continue with LinkedIn", "Continue with Apple" (AcmeCo's have no names, so screen readers say "link"). The marks in the circles are neutral placeholders: each provider's artwork is licensed only for sites that really offer its sign-in (Apple's licence also requires an Apple Developer Program membership), so it stays out of this prototype; AcmeCo's production buttons use it.

•  The carousel is a labelled region ("Why sign up"); each dot is a named button ("Slide 4 of 4: Access secure data") with a 24px target around its 8px mark (AcmeCo's are 8px buttons with no names); the current dot is marked for screen readers and is a wider pill, so it isn't shown by colour alone. Changing slides reads the new one. It never rotates by itself, so nothing moves while someone types.
•  The pictures are decorative: each slide's title and text carry its meaning.
•  The form comes first in reading order; on wide screens the promo sits to its left. On phones (full screen) the promo moves below the form.
•  Clicking outside doesn't close it (it holds a form, decision 28); Escape and Close do, and focus returns to what opened it.

sections.title: Overview
lines: An AI assistant people can type or talk to about listings. A floating launcher ("AcmeCo AI") opens a short connecting bar, then a panel with the conversation, a text box, Voice Mode and End chat; expand grows the same panel taller, with a header and a collapse button. AcmeCo doesn't have this today: it's modelled on the assistant AcmeCo runs publicly on a reference product, in AcmeCo's navy and blue, on AcmeCo's shape rule (decision 29). Prototype: replies are scripted and voice is simulated.

sections.title: When to use
lines: •  Once per page, floating near the content it helps with (search results, a listing), usually bottom right.
•  launcherSize="lg" beside the homepage search; md elsewhere.
•  Pass respond to connect it to a real service; the component handles states, focus and announcements.
•  With question, opened from elsewhere on the page: a result card's "Ask AcmeCo" (decision 45) passes { id, text }, and the assistant opens if needed and asks it. A new id asks again.

sections.title: When not to use
lines: •  Not as a replacement for search filters or the contact form: people must be able to do everything without it.
•  Not more than one per page.
•  Don't put the launcher where it covers a listing's price, title or primary action.

sections.title: Accessibility
lines: •  The launcher is a real button; the panel is a labelled region ("AcmeCo AI"), not a modal, so the page stays usable beside it.

•  The conversation is a log: screen readers hear new messages as they arrive, each starting with who it's from ("You:", "AcmeCo AI:"). When it's long enough to scroll, it can take keyboard focus for arrow-key scrolling.
•  "AcmeCo AI is thinking" is announced once; the bouncing dots are decoration.
•  The text box has a real label ("Message AcmeCo AI") and a readable placeholder; Enter sends. the reference product's placeholder is 1.8:1 and seems to be its only label.
•  Voice Mode is a toggle that announces on or off. The microphone button says what it will do ("Mute microphone" / "Unmute microphone").
•  Focus moves to the text box when the panel opens and back to the launcher when it closes. Escape collapses the panel and keeps the conversation; End chat clears it.
•  The greeting appears once (a reference product repeats it).
•  The moving edge, the dots and the fade stop for people who ask for reduced motion.

sections.title: Content
lines: •  Name: "AcmeCo AI" (the final name is AcmeCo's call).
•  Greeting: one short line that says what it can help with.
•  Replies: plain sentences; link to the listing or search rather than repeating long details.
•  Say clearly when an answer is uncertain, and never invent prices or availability.
